cards.name: Clean newsroom
cards.summary: Neutral, honest broadcast correction: a little contrast, recovered highlights, opened shadows and near-natural colour, so mixed press, phone and studio clips cut together without looking graded.
use_for: A-roll of political explainers and press conferences
Base correction under every other grade in this family
Matching mismatched agency / phone / studio sources
avoid: Treating it as a white-balance fix: correct Temperature/Tint per source first (about -15..15)
Stacking a second Lumetri Color on the same clip: add these values to the clip's existing Lumetri instead
Raising Saturation past ~115 on Indian skin tones: faces go orange
cards.keyframes_note: Static, no keyframes. Per-source matching goes on top of the same instance: Temperature -15..15 and Exposure -0.3..0.3 per camera. When every clip shares it, apply once on an adjustment layer (AE) or per clip (Premiere).

verified.note: Near-identical to the reference with slightly richer colour and the same tonal range (sat 0.54 -> 0.61), the invisible base correction it promises.

ae.note: Near-identical to the reference with slightly richer colour (saturation 0.54 -> 0.61) and the same tonal range, an invisible base correction; vs Premiere: Matches Premiere (saturation 0.54 -> 0.61 there too).

cards.name: Newsroom broadcast-safe finish
cards.summary: Last step for TV delivery: pull hot whites down a touch in Lumetri, then clamp anything above the legal level with Broadcast Colors (reduce luminance, PAL).
use_for: Bulletins and packages delivered to Indian TV channels (PAL)
Bright studio walls, white kurtas and window-lit interviews that run hot
Final pass after any grade in this family
avoid: Instagram / YouTube-only delivery: not needed and dulls highlights
Low IRE limits (90) or a Key Out mode: hard grey plateaus or holes in the picture
Grading after it: keep it last in the chain
Stacking with Video Limiter: pick one
cards.keyframes_note: Static. Premiere dropdowns are 0-based (Locale 1 = PAL, Make Color Safe 0 = Reduce Luminance); After Effects popups are 1-based (Locale 2 = PAL, 1 = Reduce Luminance). Use 100 IRE for a strict channel spec. Apply last, ideally on a top adjustment layer.

verified.note: Highlights sit a touch lower than the reference (99th-percentile luma 214 -> 205) with nothing else changed, a quiet legal-range finish as described.

ae.note: Highlights sit a little lower (98th percentile luma 201 -> 191, mean 106 -> 100) with colour unchanged, a quiet legal-range finish; vs Premiere: Same small highlight pull as Premiere.

cards.name: Documentary interview soft cinematic
cards.summary: Gentle cinematic interview look: slightly warm, highlights rolled off, shadows opened, a hint of faded blacks and a soft vignette that pulls the eye to the speaker.
use_for: Expert / witness talking heads in political explainers
avoid: Adding Premiere's Vignette effect too: the darkening doubles
Vertical reels with captions near the edges: drop the vignette (Amount 0)
Mixed-light rooms that are already warm: set Temperature 0
cards.keyframes_note: Static for the whole interview. The vignette (Amount/Midpoint/Feather) stays centred; for an off-centre speaker use Premiere's Vignette effect with Center on the face instead, and set Lumetri Amount to 0.

verified.note: Slightly warm, softly darkened corners (corner luma 129 -> 101) and rolled highlights pull the eye to the centre of the frame.

ae.note: A gentle change: highlights roll off slightly and the corners darken by about a fifth (152/130/77 -> 121/100/42), pulling the eye inward, while the warmth is not measurable on this already warm footage; vs Premiere: Renders the same as Premiere (corner and centre colours within 1 level).

cards.name: Cinematic teal-orange
cards.summary: Blockbuster split tone: base cooled, contrast up, shadows pushed teal and highlights and skin pushed warm orange, as a numeric primary grade (Lumetri Temperature + ASC CDL + per-channel Levels in Premiere, Color Balance in After Effects).
use_for: Cinematic B-roll and drone shots in documentaries
Hero / profile segments and title sequences
avoid: Straight news or fact-check footage: reads as a movie, not a record
Flags and party colours: tricolour green drifts teal and saffron goes orange-red
Faces lit from the shadow side: they turn cyan
Raising the offsets above ~0.05: the shift becomes a colour wash
cards.keyframes_note: Static. In Premiere the teal comes from Levels after the CDL: (R) Black Input 40 pulls red out of the darks and (B) / (G) Black Output 34 / 8 lift blue-green into them, while CDL Red / Blue Slope 1.15 / 0.9 keeps highlights and skin orange. On warm tungsten footage Lumetri Temperature plus CDL offsets (max +-0.05) only turn the shadows olive, never teal. For a lighter version halve the moves (Levels 20 / 4 / 17, Red Slope 1.07, Blue Slope 0.95, Temperature -8). The green lift keeps the shadows teal rather than purple (blue alone turns navy tones purple). To ease the look in on a reveal, keyframe Premiere Levels (B) Black Output [[0, 0], [1.0, 34]] or the AE Color Balance Shadow Blue and Highlight Red Balance from 0 to their values over 1 s. After Effects: the teal comes from Levels (Individual Controls) Red Input Black 0.157, Green Output Black 0.031 and Blue Output Black 0.133, so ease it in by keying Blue Output Black [[0, 0], [1.0, 0.133]].

verified.note: Now a real split tone: the darkest 15% went from warm brown (56,38,14) to dark teal (24,48,44) while highlights, skin and flowers stay warm orange (214,177,128), though the beige wall drifts slightly olive.

ae.note: Contrast is up and the highlights stay warm orange, but the shadows go olive-brown (darkest 15% at 32/26/8) instead of teal, so there is no split tone; vs Premiere: Premiere turns the same shadows dark teal (24,48,44) with its Levels move; the AE half has no teal at all.

previous.why: after_effects changed: Mirrors the Premiere-verified teal: Levels (Individual Controls) Red Input Black 40/255 with Green / Blue Output Black 8/255 and 34/255 after Lumetri Temperature -15, keeping Color Balance only for the warm mids and highlights.; not rendered again

cards.name: Warm nostalgic
cards.summary: Memory look: warm amber cast, softened contrast, faded milky blacks, lowered saturation, a soft vignette and fine mono grain.
avoid: Genuine archive film: it is already faded; use the archive_looks recipes instead
Grain above ~8 on 9:16 reels: it turns to mush after Instagram compression
Already-warm tungsten interiors: drop Temperature to ~12
cards.keyframes_note: Drifting into the memory: keyframe Lumetri Temperature [[0, 0], [1.0, 28]] and Faded Film [[0, 0], [1.0, 30]] from the first frame of the section, under a 1 s Film Dissolve from the present-day shot. Grain needs no keyframes (it re-randomises every frame). AE grain uses Add Grain (Viewing Mode 3 = Final Output is mandatory; the default Preview shows grain only inside a box); it is slow, so put it on one adjustment layer.

verified.note: Milky lifted blacks, softer contrast, muted amber colour and clearly darkened corners give a faded memory look; the fine grain is barely visible at this size.

ae.note: Softer contrast (luma spread 46 -> 39), milky blacks with the blue lifted (darkest tones 59/41/32 vs 63/42/21), lower saturation (0.54 -> 0.46), darker corners and fine grain give a faded memory look with a muted amber-pink cast; vs Premiere: Renders the same as Premiere apart from the grain.

cards.name: Golden hope
cards.summary: Clean, warm, vivid optimism: golden temperature, a touch of exposure, crisp contrast and richer colour without any fade.
use_for: Achievement and development B-roll (roads, launches, inaugurations)
Upbeat explainer outros and social reels
avoid: Night or tungsten-lit footage: goes orange
Saffron/brand-heavy frames: colours oversaturate and clip
Serious or tragic segments: the warmth reads as celebratory
cards.keyframes_note: Static. For a 'dawn' lift on a hopeful line keyframe Temperature [[0, 0], [1.5, 22]] and Exposure [[0, -0.3], [1.5, 0.15]] from the hit.

verified.note: Visibly more golden and saturated than the reference (R 129 -> 142, B 63 -> 48) with crisp contrast and no fade.

ae.note: Visibly more golden and saturated (mean 128/102/62 -> 141/101/47, saturation 0.54 -> 0.69) with crisp contrast and no fade; vs Premiere: Matches Premiere (R 129 -> 142, B 63 -> 48 there).

cards.name: Cold tense
cards.summary: Suspense grade: drains the warm cast to a cold, muted grey with blue-teal blacks, slightly under-exposed, deeper shadows and a firm vignette; on warm tungsten footage it reads cold-neutral, not a strong blue-cyan cast.
avoid: Talking heads that must look trustworthy: skin goes grey-blue
Brand and flag colours: saffron dulls to brown
Combining with Day-for-night: double blue and too dark
cards.keyframes_note: Creeping dread: keyframe Lumetri Temperature [[0, 0], [3.0, -28]] and Saturation [[0, 100], [3.0, 72]] across the build, then hold. Levels are 8-bit in Premiere (32 / 14) and normalised in After Effects (32/255 = 0.125, 14/255 = 0.055); 12 / 6 left the blacks warm on tungsten footage.

verified.note: Teal blacks now read (34,33,27 -> 35,40,45) and it is darker, muted (sat 0.27 -> 0.19) and vignetted, but the mids and highlights stay neutral-beige (mean 92,90,82), so it reads cold grey rather than blue-cyan; summary made honest.

ae.note: Darker, muted (saturation 0.54 -> 0.19) cold-neutral grey with blue-teal blacks (35/39/45) and a firm vignette, cold grey rather than blue as the summary says; vs Premiere: Practically identical to Premiere (blacks 35,40,45 and mean 92,90,82 there).

cards.name: Noir high-contrast
cards.summary: Hard black-and-white: full desaturation, steep contrast with crushed-but-not-dead blacks and bright whites, crisp detail, a heavy vignette and fine mono grain.
use_for: Era change into a historical section
avoid: Blacks below ~-40: shadow detail vanishes after platform compression
Footage where colour carries meaning (flags, party colours, maps)
Using Premiere's Black & White effect for an animated change: it has no controls; keyframe Lumetri Saturation instead
cards.keyframes_note: Colour-to-noir on a hit: Premiere Lumetri Saturation [[0, 100], [0.8, 0]] from the hit; in After Effects keyframe Lumetri Saturation the same way and leave Black & White off (or fade its layer). The AE Black & White weights keep skin light and darken blue skies like a red filter. AE grain uses Add Grain (Viewing Mode 3 = Final Output is mandatory; the default Preview shows grain only inside a box); it is slow, so put it on one adjustment layer.

verified.note: Full black-and-white with steep contrast, deep but detailed blacks, bright whites and a heavy vignette.

ae.note: Full black-and-white with steep contrast (luma spread 46 -> 58), deep but detailed blacks, bright whites, darkened corners and fine grain; vs Premiere: Matches Premiere, slightly brighter (mean luma 102 vs 94).

cards.name: Desaturated war
cards.summary: Bleach-bypass style conflict grade: colour drained to about 40%, hard contrast, a faint olive-green cast, gritty sharpening, a dark vignette and mono grain.
avoid: Real casualty or atrocity footage: do not stylise it
Faces that must stay identifiable and natural: skin goes sallow
Grain above ~8 on reels
cards.keyframes_note: Static. On an explosion or impact hit, flash Lumetri Exposure [[0, 0], [0.06, 1.2], [0.3, 0]] on top of the grade. AE grain uses Add Grain (Viewing Mode 3 = Final Output is mandatory; the default Preview shows grain only inside a box); it is slow, so put it on one adjustment layer.

verified.note: Colour drained to about half with hard contrast, a faint olive cast and a dark vignette, a clear bleach-bypass conflict look.

ae.note: Colour drained to under half (saturation 0.54 -> 0.25), hard contrast, a faint olive shift, gritty grain and a dark vignette: a bleach-bypass conflict look; vs Premiere: Practically identical to Premiere (mean 99,89,76 vs 99,89,77).

cards.name: Saffron colour splash
cards.summary: Drains the frame to grey and keeps only the tones closest to bright saffron #FF9933; on the dim test plate that is just a few orange specks (flower petals), so sample the real flag colour into Color before relying on the flag staying in colour.
use_for: Rally and campaign footage where the saffron must lead
avoid: Faces: skin hue sits next to saffron, so faces stay partly coloured and patchy; sample the real flag colour and keep Similarity / Tolerance low
Factual news footage: selective colour editorialises
Compressed phone footage: the kept colour's edges flicker
cards.keyframes_note: Colour drains away except saffron: Premiere Color Pass Similarity [[0, 120], [1.0, 25]], After Effects Leave Color Amount to Decolor [[0, 0], [1.0, 92]], starting on the beat. Replace #FF9933 with the colour sampled from the actual flag for a clean key. At Similarity 18 a bright #FF9933 matched nothing on the dim test plate and the whole frame went grey; 25 keeps the saffron-orange tones only.

verified.note: No longer fully grey: a few orange flower petals and a stray yellow wall patch keep colour (sat 0.000 -> 0.006), but the plate's own saffron area and the rest of the frame stay grey, so it is a speck splash, not a saffron one; summary made honest.

ae.note: Nothing drains: both frames keep full colour (saturation 0.54 -> 0.57, mean difference 3 levels), because Leave Color matching by hue treats the whole warm tungsten frame as close to #FF9933; vs Premiere: Premiere drains the frame to grey with only a few orange petals left; the AE half stays in full colour.

previous.why: after_effects changed: Matching by RGB (Match colors 1) instead of hue should keep only the bright saffron-orange pixels in colour, as Premiere's Color Pass does, instead of every warm-hued pixel.; not rendered again

cards.name: Saffron brand warm grade
cards.summary: Brand-tinted warmth: golden-saffron temperature and richer colour, with a soft saffron glow creeping in from the frame edges (Premiere).
use_for: Party / campaign brand reels and promos
Title, logo and slogan beats over footage
avoid: News or fact-check footage: a brand tint reads as propaganda
Stacking with Lumetri's own vignette (Amount): double edge
Vertical reels with captions at the edges: drop the Vignette opacity to ~30
cards.keyframes_note: Bloom the saffron edge in on a title or logo beat: Premiere Vignette Master [[0, 0], [0.6, 100]]. After Effects has no coloured-edge vignette in one effect, so its version adds an even amber warmth (Photo Filter, Warming 85) instead; keyframe Density [[0, 0], [0.6, 15]] for the same bloom. Vignette Scale above ~100 pushes the edge off-frame: at Scale 105-110 with Vignette 40-55 the coloured edge did not show at all, so keep Scale 75-80.

verified.note: The saffron glow now shows: all four edges bloom orange (corners 161,122,55 -> 197,127,51) around the same warm golden grade, which is the brand look the summary promises.

ae.note: Warmer golden-saffron colour (mean 128/102/62 -> 136/96/46, saturation 0.54 -> 0.68) with an even amber cast and no edge glow, which the summary scopes to Premiere; vs Premiere: Same warm grade as Premiere without its orange edge bloom.

cards.name: Day-for-night
cards.summary: Fake night from daylight: about 1.5 stops under, strong blue moonlight cast, sky and highlights pulled down hard, colour reduced and heavy dark edges.
use_for: Night scenes in reconstructions built from daylight B-roll
avoid: Visible sun, bright sky or hard daylight shadows: they give it away
Faces in direct sun
Combining with Cold tense: too dark and too blue
cards.keyframes_note: Static. Color Balance (RGB) units are 0..510 with 255 neutral, so 180/235/360 equal the AE gains 0.71/0.92/1.41 (the milder 225/240/285 left warm footage neutral grey, not blue). For a dusk-to-night fall keyframe Exposure [[0, 0], [2.0, -1.5]] and Temperature [[0, 0], [2.0, -40]].
cards.notes: Optional upgrade by hand: the SpeedLooks 'Blue Day4Nite' look (Lumetri Creative > Look, or the SL Blue Day4Nite preset) gives a richer moonlight, but a spec cannot select a LUT; apply it manually and drop Temperature to about -15.

verified.note: Now a blue moonlight night instead of grey: mean 42,41,40 -> 33,40,50 with blue highlights (61,74,99), about 1.5 stops down with heavy dark edges.

ae.note: About 1.4 stops darker (mean luma 106 -> 40) with a blue moonlight cast (33/40/50), reduced colour and heavy dark edges; vs Premiere: Practically identical to Premiere (33,40,50 there).

cards.name: Promise-to-reality swing
cards.summary: Animated grade change on one shot: warm, saturated 'promise' swings to a cold, muted, harder 'reality' over about a second.
use_for: 'But the reality is...' turns in political explainers
Before / after and claim vs fact segments
avoid: Using it on every claim: the move loses its punch after two or three uses per video
Shots with faces in close-up during the swing: skin visibly changes colour
cards.keyframes_note: Times are relative to the hit word ('but', 'reality'): the swing starts on it and lands 1.0 s later, sub_drop on the hit. Across a cut instead of within one shot, use the end values as static grades: promise clips Temperature 22 / Saturation 112 / Contrast 12, reality clips -22 / 72 / 26.

verified.note: 0.2 s frame is warm and saturated, 1.0 s frame is cold, muted and harder (sat 0.64 -> 0.36, B 53 -> 79), the swing lands as described.

ae.note: 0.2 s is warm and saturated (saturation 0.63) and 1.0 s is cold, muted and harder (saturation 0.35, blue 79), so the swing lands as described; vs Premiere: Matches Premiere (saturation 0.64 -> 0.36, B 53 -> 79 there).

cards.name: Crisis red edge
cards.summary: Alarm grade for breaking or crisis beats: cool, muted, contrasty picture with a red glow pressing in from the frame edges.
avoid: Holding it for long sections: it tires fast; use it for 2-6 s beats
Captions near the frame edges on 9:16
Sensitive tragedy footage where the red reads as sensational
cards.keyframes_note: Pulse the red edge with the heartbeat: Premiere Vignette Master [[0, 0], [0.12, 100], [0.6, 60], [0.9, 100], [1.4, 60]]. After Effects has no coloured-edge vignette effect, so its version uses a dark Lumetri vignette; keyframe Amount [[0, 0], [0.12, -1.2]] for the same hit. Vignette Scale above ~100 pushes the edge off-frame: at Scale 105-110 with Vignette 40-55 the coloured edge did not show at all, so keep Scale 75-80. After Effects: the red edge is the inverted Circle, so pulse it by keying its Opacity [[0, 0], [0.12, 70], [0.6, 42], [0.9, 70], [1.4, 42]] rather than Lumetri Amount.

verified.note: The red alarm edge now presses in from both sides (corners 140,114,88 -> 164,31,50) around a muted, contrasty, slightly cooled centre.

ae.note: A cool, muted, contrasty picture with slightly darkened edges but no red anywhere (corners 100/88/55), so the red alarm edge the summary promises is missing; vs Premiere: Premiere's corners go red (164,31,50); the AE half only darkens them.

previous.why: after_effects changed: An inverted, feathered red Circle (#C8102E, Opacity 70, Normal blend) after the grade adds the red edge pressing in from the sides and corners that Lumetri's vignette cannot colour.; not rendered again

cards.name: Punchy social
cards.summary: Clean, vivid feed-ready grade: more contrast and vibrance, held highlights, a little sharpening, with skin kept natural.
use_for: Instagram and YouTube Shorts versions of news and explainers
avoid: Saturation above ~140: skin goes orange and colours clip after upload
Heavily compressed footage: sharpening and vibrance reveal blocking
Long-form documentaries: too loud

verified.note: Cleanly more vivid and contrasty than the reference (sat 0.54 -> 0.67) with held highlights and skin still natural.

ae.note: Cleanly more vivid and contrasty (saturation 0.54 -> 0.67) with held highlights and nothing clipped; vs Premiere: Matches Premiere (saturation 0.54 -> 0.67 there).
